Bug_Title: EC: equals(…) used to compare incompatible arrays (EC_INCOMPATIBLE_ARRAY_COMPARE)
Bug_Details:
This method invokes the .equals(Object o) to compare two arrays, but the arrays
of incompatible types (e.g., String[] and StringBuffer[], or String[] and int[]).
They will never be equal. In addition, when equals(...) is used to compare arrays it
only checks to see if they are the same array, and ignores the contents of the arrays.
Bug_Explanation: This Java code demonstrates a bug related to the equals method. The equals method is used to compare two arrays, but in the given code the arrays are of incompatible types (String[] and StringBuffer[]). The equals method only checks if the arrays are the same array, and it ignores the contents of the arrays. Therefore, the result is incorrect.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUNIT test case triggered the bug by using the `Arrays.equals()` method on incompatible arrays, specifically `String[]` and `StringBuffer[]`. The `Arrays.equals()` method uses `==` for comparison, which means it checks if the arrays are the same instance. Since `String[]` and `StringBuffer[]` are not the same class, they will never be equal. Therefore, the test fails and triggers the bug.
